key_insight: An additive thermodynamic correction layer aligns machine learning interatomic potentials with assessed phase equilibria without retraining or modifying the base model.
engineering_relevance: The approach improves transformation-temperature predictions for atomistic materials simulations while largely preserving the base model’s static mechanical and liquid-structure predictions.
method: Convert required phase free-energy shifts into configuration energy targets using a first-order thermodynamic construction.
Fit an additive correction with a linear atomic cluster expansion.
Iteratively refine the correction using measured free energies.
evidence_signal: Tests with a foundation GRACE model brought all studied transformation temperatures within prescribed tolerances, including simultaneous solid–solid and melting corrections for Ca, Ti, and Zr.
watch_item: Large corrections can alter vacancy formation energies, thermal expansion, and liquid density, so these properties require validation.
paper_title: A thermodynamic correction layer for machine learning interatomic potentials
